WT_PROJECT_ID.description: Optional watchTowr project identifier forwarded server-side as the project_id query param on /api/v1/asset-inventory and /api/v1/findings. Service-account API keys with cross-project scope may omit it; otherwise set to the watchTowr project identifier shown in the console URL. Defaults to '' (no project scope; watchTowr returns whatever the key has access to).

WT_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional severity floor applied client-side on the findings surface. Accepts the canonical Faraday enum (info / low / medium / high / critical) plus watchTowr-side aliases (Important / Major / Moderate / Informational / Negligible / Sev1..Sev5 / P1..P5). Defaults to '' (no filter; we emit the full hits surface). Garbage values are logged and ignored.

WT_PAGES.description: Optional per-surface page-walk cap. Each watchTowr v1 search page returns up to 100 hits via limit=100; WT_PAGES bounds the offset walk so a stray operator filter can't fan out into 100k+ requests against the rate-limited watchTowr API. Numeric / numeric-string input accepted; floats are floored. Clamped to [1, 50]. Defaults to 5 (~ 500 hits per surface, 1000 total across asset-inventory + findings).

name: watchtowr
title: watchTowr
description: watchTowr EASM importer. Pulls externally-discovered assets and findings from the watchTowr REST API and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Each watchTowr asset becomes one Faraday host (ip = the asset's first public IP, falling back to synthetic 0.0.0.0 for domain-keyed assets); per-asset findings attach as one Faraday vulnerability per finding_id with the [EASM] engine prefix. Endpoints used: GET /api/v1/asset-inventory (paginated external-asset inventory; the canonical watchTowr pivot - every finding joins by asset_id) and GET /api/v1/findings (paginated finding inventory with severity + category + cves + remediation guidance; query string also carries the operator-supplied project_id so watchTowr narrows server-side). Pagination is offset-based: limit=100 per page, offset advanced via the response envelope's next_offset cursor (or current_offset + page_size when the envelope is silent), walked page-by-page until the page comes up short or WT_PAGES is reached. Severity bucketing walks the string severity field first (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info) and falls back to priority / risk_rating / risk_score (watchTowr 0-10 scale) then CVSS when nothing else lands; aliases collapse watchTowr-side labels (Important / Major / Moderate / Informational / Negligible / Sev1..Sev5 / P1..P5) onto the canonical Faraday bucket. Status mapping covers new / in_progress / investigating / triaged -> open, resolved / closed / remediated / fixed / mitigated / patched -> closed, and false_positive / risk_accepted / accepted_risk / wont_fix -> risk-accepted. Refs include watchTowr-Asset / watchTowr-AssetName / watchTowr-AssetType / watchTowr-Project / watchTowr-Id / watchTowr-Category / watchTowr-Port pivots plus any url / reference_url / evidence_url surfaced on the finding. Auth: watchTowr uses a single long-lived API key created in the watchTowr console under Settings -> API Keys -> New. The dispatcher carries the key on every request as the Authorization: Bearer <WT_API_KEY> header. WT_HOST is the watchTowr tenant host (e.g. api.watchtowr.com); service-account keys carry the tenant scope so no workspace param is required. Tags: [watchtowr, easm].
